note: People, institutions and organizations whose work on portable funding is on the record. Each entry has a source. 'year' is when the work began, where verified. Policy organizations (added 10 Nov 2026) appear for the research and model policy they publish, coded 'studies it' alike; inclusion records a role, not an endorsement.

leaders.name: Arizona State University
leaders.what: Runs university-owned K–12 schools and an online school that accepts Arizona ESA funds; expanding into Texas.

leaders.name: University of Notre Dame
leaders.what: Runs Notre Dame ACE Academies, a network of Catholic K–8 schools that includes a school in the Diocese of St. Petersburg, and staffs Catholic schools through ACE Teaching Fellows.

leaders.name: Florida Virtual School
leaders.what: Hosts teaching internships for students from 40 partner colleges and universities. Non-district clinical placement already works at scale.

leaders.name: University of Florida
leaders.what: Runs P.K. Yonge Developmental Research School, a public PreK–12 lab school whose teachers are university employees. UF Lastinger also vetted private tutoring vendors for the state's public-school tutoring program.

leaders.name: Tallahassee State College
leaders.what: First Florida College System institution approved to authorize charter schools; founded Tallahassee Collegiate Academy.

leaders.name: Central Michigan University
leaders.what: The only preparation program built for the sector across all eight Michigan university charter authorizers.

leaders.name: University of Pennsylvania
leaders.what: A two-year residency placing fellows in independent schools; 19 boarding and day schools list openings for 2027–28.

leaders.name: Rio Salado College
leaders.what: About 9,700 dual-enrollment students; 200 of the 408 on track for associate degrees attend one charter network, Heritage Academy.

leaders.name: University of Central Florida
leaders.what: 43 Community Partnership Schools inside existing public schools; state funding nearly doubled in 2024.

leaders.name: Julie Young
leaders.org: Florida Virtual School, then ASU Prep
leaders.what: Founded Florida Virtual School, then led ASU Prep. One career carried a portable model across two states.

leaders.name: Keith Parker
leaders.what: Opened a 26-student public microschool designed after visits to 40+ schools, including private microschools.

leaders.name: Polk County Public Schools
leaders.what: Bought a microschool model from a private operator founded by two former Polk teachers.

leaders.name: Miami-Dade County Public Schools
leaders.what: Opened more than 95 classes to students it does not enroll.

leaders.name: St. Vrain Valley Schools
leaders.what: Runs a homeschool enrichment program with more than 700 students; about 30 of Colorado's 179 districts offer one.

leaders.name: Indiana Microschool Collaborative
leaders.what: A charter network of public microschools launched by a district superintendent, aiming for at least 10 more schools by 2030.

leaders.name: Douglas Harris
leaders.org: Tulane University · REACH and ERA-New Orleans
leaders.what: Among the leaders of REACH, a $10M federally funded national center for research on school choice.

leaders.name: Paul E. Peterson
leaders.what: Hosts Education Next's podcast, which covers ESAs and their effect on public schools.

leaders.name: Kevin Welner
leaders.org: CU Boulder · National Education Policy Center
leaders.what: Directs the National Education Policy Center (NEPC), which publishes third-party reviews of think-tank reports, including school-choice studies.

leaders.name: Christopher Lubienski
leaders.what: Studies how schools respond to competition in local education markets; co-author of The Public School Advantage.

leaders.name: Angela R. Watson
leaders.what: Built the Homeschool Hub at Johns Hopkins; researches homeschool and informal learning options.

leaders.name: EdChoice
leaders.what: Published The Supply Side of ESAs (2025), on how universal programs changed the number of private schools and home-education vendors.

leaders.name: ExcelinEd
leaders.what: Publishes model policies on the teacher pipeline, including teacher apprenticeships, educator supply-and-demand dashboards and state-approved “chartered teachers” who contract directly with families.

leaders.name: Cato Institute, Center for Educational Freedom
leaders.what: Researches and argues for education choice; says education works best when learners and educators choose freely.

leaders.name: Center for Education Reform
leaders.what: Works on charter schools and other education choice; founded by Jeanne Allen.

leaders.name: National Education Association
leaders.what: Opposes vouchers, arguing they move public school funding to private schools with less accountability.

leaders.name: American Federation of Teachers
leaders.what: Adopted “Keep Public Funds for Public Schools: Oppose Vouchers” on 19 July 2026.

leaders.name: Learning Policy Institute
leaders.what: Published a 2024 fiscal analysis of Arizona's universal ESA program, finding a $587.5 million cost in its first universal year.

leaders.name: Network for Public Education
leaders.what: Grades all 50 states and D.C. on support for public schools, including private choice programs and teaching conditions (2026 Report Card).

leaders.name: AACTE
leaders.org: American Association of Colleges for Teacher Education
leaders.what: The national association of colleges and universities that prepare teachers, counselors and school leaders: the institutions this site measures.

leaders.name: NCTQ
leaders.what: Reviews teacher preparation programs against published standards in its Teacher Prep Review.

leaders.name: NACSA
leaders.org: National Association of Charter School Authorizers
leaders.what: Works with charter school authorizers, the role several Florida colleges and universities now hold.
